author: claude
subject: Thread verdict
body:
The contract implements the approved specification, and three elements are stronger than what was asked for.

**Budgets are declared, not merely compared.** `harness/performance/live-v5.toml` pins `backend_requests_per_operation` per workload — 49, 43, 15, 18, 10 — and `requests_per_entry_scanned = 4.0` on every flat listing case. A deviation now fails against a stated constant rather than against a prior campaign, so the first v5 run can fail closed instead of merely establishing. Part F of the specification stated those values as predictions to be checked by hand; they are now assertions the runner enforces.

**`"establish"` is the honest treatment of what is genuinely unknown.** `put_block_sequence`, `get_block_list` and `list_containers` carry it because no measurement exists. Declaring a guessed constant there would have been worse than declaring nothing.

**Latency gating is derived per case, per target, per campaign.** `compare_live_performance.py:134` requires `p50Classification == "blocking"` on all four of current gateway, baseline gateway, current direct and baseline direct before a latency comparison can fail a gate; otherwise it degrades to `signal`. The specification asked that the classification be derived from measurement rather than declared. This goes further: it requires unanimity across both campaigns and both targets, and it compares medians of the three per-run p50 values rather than a single point.

**Request counts use strict equality** at line 125 for schema ≥ 4 — `current_requests == baseline_requests`. Any change fails, including a reduction. That is the correct reading: an optimisation that removes a round trip must rebase the budget deliberately and justify it, rather than sliding under a `<=` comparison. It is also what will happen the day the lock change lands, and it should not be softened then.

**Listing instrumentation costs nothing.** `gateway/src/listing.rs` adds a `u64` counter incremented in the existing loop and one field on the response struct; emission happens once per request in `gateway/src/app.rs`. Both branches of the container loop increment, so every candidate is counted once. There is no per-entry logging on the path being measured, which would have been self-defeating.

**Server-side aggregation preserves exactness where it is gated.** The Log Analytics query counts with `count()`, distinguishes unattributed requests with `countif(isempty(Fingerprint) or Fingerprint == 'missing')`, and uses `count_distinct` rather than the approximate `dcount` for client request counts. The gated quantities remain exact integers.

One consequence to record: `responseHeadersDuration` percentiles are now computed with KQL `percentile()`, which is an approximation by design. Those fields are diagnostic and ungated, so nothing depends on them — but they should be labelled as approximate in the bundle, and they should not be compared against earlier campaigns if those computed them differently.

**One item to settle before the campaign runs.** `p50_stability_spread_ratio_threshold = 1.10` is a value chosen before the data that determines it exists. The v4 campaign's `resolution` block was produced precisely to establish the run-to-run spread, and its results are not yet imported. If the measured spreads sit above 1.10 — which the v2-to-v3 comparison suggests is plausible for read cases — then no case will qualify and the latency gate will be silently inert, degrading to `signal` without anything reporting that it never engaged.

The mechanism is right; only the number is provisional. Set it from v4's `resolution` once imported, and consider recording in the bundle how many cases actually qualified for latency gating, so that an inert gate is visible rather than assumed.

**What this verdict does not cover.** Methods: source review only. No commands executed; no cargo toolchain is available in this environment. Seq 3 names `make test-pr`, `make performance-contract-check`, `az bicep build` and `cargo fmt --check`, and those runs are unconfirmed here and falsifiable by anyone who repeats them.
